title: Starter engagement credit cartography
content:
Goal: sketch a lightweight starter plan that nudges new signups to meaningful usage quickly without destroying unit economics. Focus: conversational apps + embeddings pilots.

High-level hypothesis:
- Give a small bucket of engagement credits tied to 'meaningful interactions' (not raw tokens) to accelerate product/market fit.
- Credits should decay or amortize so long-tail free riders don't eat infra.
- Link credits to activation milestones (1st integration, 1st embed call, first 100 tokens of structured output).

Terminology (quick, unpolished):
- credit = currency we give on signup (1 credit ~= N tokens for chat; but convertible rules vary by feature).
- convo-unit = one conversational session up to 2k tokens of generation (approx).
- embed-unit = 1k embedding vectors produced (batch semantics apply).

Assumptions to test (back-of-envelope):
- avg convo call uses 300 generated tokens (prompt+response).
- hosted infra cost per 1k tokens generated = $0.004 (weighted avg across models we surface to starter users).
- embeddings cost per 1k vectors = $0.02 (ballpark for smaller model or quantized flow).
- desired starter NPV per free user <= $2.50 (we expect conversion or upsell).

Simple conversion from credits to dollars (proto):
- Set 100 starter credits.
- mapping: 1 convo-unit = 1 credit (assume covers avg 300 tokens -> ~$0.0012 infra cost), 1 embed-unit = 5 credits (covers batch of 1k vectors -> ~$0.02 infra cost).
- If avg activation uses 3 convos + 1 embed batch -> consumes ~8 credits -> infra cost ~ $0.005 -> very cheap. Good.

But big gotcha: bursty power users can hit model choices (bigger model). Add policy: credits redeem against 'starter-tier models' only; if a request routes to larger model, premium charge applies or credits consume faster (x3).

Decay & timeboxing mechanics (ideas):
- Option A: credits expire after 90 days. Simple, enforces quick activation.
- Option B: credits half-life (50% useable after 30d, etc) — more complex. Probably too heavy for first pass.
- Option C: session-limited credits: first 30 sessions free-ish, but throttle per minute after. Messy, avoid.

Activation milestones to gate extra credit grants:
- connect data source (docs upload, DB): +50 credits (one-time).
- open-source SDK usage with repo link verified: +20 credits.
- invite collaborator (team virality): +10 credits per invite (cap 30).
Rationale: tie incremental credits to high-quality signals (higher chance to convert).

Unit economics quick math: (target mature conversion: 5% paid, CAC baked into acquisition budget separately)
- Give 100 credits on signup (cost to us if fully consumed depends on mix).
- Worst-case model mix: 20% heavy model requests -> effective unit cost per starter = $1.20.
- Expected mix (mostly small models) -> unit cost per starter = $0.18.
- So plan: cap promotional exposure to heavy models (either block or require billable add-on).

Edge cases & fraud vectors:
- Multiple accounts to farm credits — mitigate by phone/email verification + device fingerprint + limits on credit grant by IP heuristics.
- Batch ingestion for embeddings (heavy cost) — limit embedding batch size or mark first-of-kind calls as non-credit-eligible.
- Abuse via large function-calls (code-gen) — detect pattern and surface upgrade CTA instead of free credits.

Open questions (prioritized):
1) What conversion signal do we want to optimize for? (first paid invoice vs. usage above X over 30 days).
2) Do we allow credits on private/dedicated trials? (probably only hosted API).
3) How to handle refunds/chargebacks if credits used then cancelled?
4) Instrumentation: need per-credit redemption telemetry -> route, model, token-count, user cohort. (Important for ROI and fraud detection)

Experimental buckets (A/B ideas):
- A: 100 credits + 90d expiry (baseline).
- B: 100 credits + 50 credits unlocked only after connecting a data source (pushes integration).
- C: 50 credits + wider model access for first 7 days (test whether access breadth increases perceived value).
Metrics to track: activation-rate (key events), 7d usage retention, conversion to paid within 60d, average infra cost per credited user, fraud rate.

Implementation notes (engineering):
- Credits ledger service -> lightweight table: user_id, credit_bucket, issued_at, expires_at, source_tag, consumed_at, consumption_reason. Keep schema small.
- Redemption service should prefer cheap-model variants; routing policy: try starter-optimized model family; if customer requests heavy model, surface warning and clawback? (product question).
- UI: credit meter on dashboard + tooltips about model-class consumption.

Quick sketches of UI copy:
- "Welcome! You have 100 Starter Credits — good for ~30 conversations with our compact models. Connect a data source to unlock 50 bonus credits."
- When a request would consume premium credits: red pill: "Heads up — this request will use Premium Credits. Continue?"

Next steps (my todo):
- Run small sims with existing user telemetry to estimate real avg convo tokens (ask Ethan for sample: event stream convo_token_count last 90d).
- Create a JIRA ticket for credits ledger prototype (JIRA-PRIC-789?).
- Wire up a minimal experiment: bucket new signups for 4 weeks only, measure conversion.
- Draft support/FAQ snippet for credit expiry, fraud policy.

Rough timeline: prototype in 4 sprints (ledger + routing + dashboard), experiment live in 8–10 weeks.

Loose behavioral heuristics for product: credits should feel generous but not a free pass. Aim for 2–5 meaningful engagements. Instrument to know whether we delivered that.

Quick raw numbers table (for reference, rough):
- Starter credits: 100
- Avg convo tokens: 300 -> cost per convo ~ $0.0012
- Embedding batch cost: 5x convo (mapping) -> ~ $0.006
- Expected starter infra cost (per active user who exhausts credits): $0.5 (highly variable)

Notes-to-self: keep the mapping abstract (credits -> unit types) flexible. Avoid hardcoding token conversion at first release; implement consumption rules as "conversion functions" in ledger service.
